abstract: AIM: The objective of this study was to evaluate the utility of CD34-positive peripheral blood stem cell transplantation (PBSCT) in the hematopoietic recovery, in patients receiving high-dose chemotherapy (HDCT), for advanced germ cell tumor (GCT). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study included 41 patients with advanced GCT, who were treated with HTCT combined with PBSCT. PBSCs were harvested after conditioning chemotherapy followed by the administration of granulocyte colony-stimulating factor. A retrospective analysis of a total of 86 PBSCTs was carried out focusing on the effects of several factors, including age (<35 years versus > or = 35 years), CD34-positive cell dose (<5.0 x10(6)/kg versus > or =5.0 x10(6)/kg), indication of HDCT (first-line versus salvage) and previous history of HDCT before PBSCT (with versus without), on hematopoietic recovery after PBSCT. RESULTS: The median number of CD34-positive PBSCs collected during a single apheresis and the median cumulative number of CD34-positive PBSCs from each patient were 8.3x10(6)/kg and 23.2x10(6)/kg, respectively. The median number of PBSCT performed in each patient was two and the median number of CD34-positive cells transplanted during a single course was 5.7x10(6)/kg. The median recovery times to white blood cells (WBC) greater than 500/microl, 1000/microl and 2000/microl were 8, 9 and 10 days, respectively, following PBSCT, while that to neutrophils greater than 500/microl and that to platelets greater than 50000/microl were 9 and 13 days, respectively, following PBSCT Only the recovery time to platelet count greater than 50000/microl was significantly affected by age; however, there were no significant differences in the recovery of WBC, neutrophils and platelets in relation to several parameters examined. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that CD34-positive PBSCT may facilitate stable hematopoietic recovery after HDCT in patients with advanced GCT, and that HDCT, if combined with PBSCT, could be performed with comparative safety in such patients, irrespective of their individual characteristics.
abstract_ja: 目的：進行期胚細胞腫瘍(GCT)に対する大量化学療法(HDCT)と併用した末梢血幹細胞移植(PBSCT)における造血回復の有用性を評価すること。対象と方法：進行期GCT患者41例を対象とし、PBSCTを併用したHDCTを施行した。PBSCTは、前処置化学療法の後に顆粒球コロニー刺激因子(G-CSF)を投与して採取した。PBSCT計86回の後方視的解析を行い、年齢(35歳未満と35歳以上)、CD34陽性細胞量(5.0×10^6/kg未満と以上)、HDCTの適応(初回治療か救済治療か)、PBSCT前のHDCT歴(あり・なし)の影響を検討した。結果：単回アフェレーシスで採取されたCD34陽性PBSCの中央値は8.3×10^6/kgで、各患者から採取されたCD34陽性PBSCの累積中央値は23.2×10^6/kgであった。各患者に施行されたPBSCTの中央値は2回で、1コースあたり移植されたCD34陽性細胞の中央値は5.7×10^6/kgであった。白血球500/μL、1000/μL、2000/μLを超えるまでの回復時間の中央値は、PBSCT後それぞれ8日、9日、10日であった。好中球500/μL超および血小板50000/μL超までの回復時間の中央値は、PBSCT後それぞれ9日、13日であった。血小板数が50000/μLを超えるまでの回復時間のみが年齢の影響を有意に受けたが、検討したその他のパラメータに関して白血球、好中球、血小板の回復に有意差はなかった。結論：CD34陽性PBSCTは進行期GCT患者においてHDCT後の安定した造血回復を促進する可能性があり、HDCTをPBSCTと併用すれば、個々の患者特性にかかわらず比較的安全に施行できると考えられる。
